nodes.title: Configure the five shapes
nodes.summary: Define each shape with an id, label, fields (key, label, default, min, max) and a geometry function that returns the SVG element data and its bounding size in mm. Support Circle, Square, Rectangle, Triangle (equilateral, point up) and Polygon (regular, sized by circumscribed diameter, 3 to 64 whole-number sides). Open decisions on triangle input, polygon sizing and polygon orientation need confirming.

nodes.title: Render shapes at true mm size
nodes.summary: Use SVG units of 1 unit = 1 mm, with width and height in mm and the viewBox computed from the shape's min and max points. Compute regular polygon points with a shared helper (also used for the triangle), draw outlines without changing the stated size and document the stroke approach, and use the CSS variable colours so dark mode works.

nodes.title: Implement selector and input behaviour
nodes.summary: Changing the dropdown swaps the input fields and redraws immediately, and each shape remembers its last-entered values. Redraw on every keystroke, show an inline message for empty, zero, negative or out-of-range input instead of rendering or showing NaN, keep wide shapes scrolling inside the drawing area, and keep the pixel-density note.

nodes.title: Meet accessibility, testing and responsiveness standards
nodes.summary: Label every input, announce errors with role="alert", keep an updating SVG aria-label and visible focus states. Add unit tests for the geometry functions (bounding sizes, polygon point counts, triangle height) and stack the panel above the drawing area on narrow screens.

nodes.title: Satisfy the acceptance criteria
nodes.summary: Each of the five shapes renders at the entered mm size when checked with a ruler or screen measurement tool, and the page loads with Circle at 20 mm. Switching shapes and back keeps earlier values, invalid input never breaks the page, and light and dark mode both work.
